name: Guest_friendship
definition: Two Partners (Partner_1 and Partner_2, or jointly Partners), normally members of different communities, are bound in a lasting and reciprocal relationship of ritualised friendship (Greek xenia). The bond is typically created when one Partner receives the other as a guest and the two exchange gifts (Token); it outlasts the visit, may be inherited by the Partners' descendants (Origin_of_bond), and obliges each Partner to receive, protect and help the other or the other's kin whenever they come, under the sanction of a Guarantor deity. Unlike Guest_and_host, the relationship is not temporary and both Partners can play either role; unlike Personal_relationship, it is defined by hospitality and gift exchange rather than by affection or kinship.

core_FEs.name: Partner_1
core_FEs.definition: One of the two guest-friends, when the Partners are expressed separately.

core_FEs.name: Partner_2
core_FEs.definition: The other guest-friend, when the Partners are expressed separately.

core_FEs.name: Partners
core_FEs.definition: Both guest-friends expressed together (often with a reciprocal pronoun).

noncore_FEs.name: Origin_of_bond
noncore_FEs.definition: How or through whom the bond arose, e.g. inherited from the Partners' fathers (πατρώιος) or begun by a particular visit.

noncore_FEs.name: Token
noncore_FEs.definition: The gift(s) exchanged that create, renew or attest the bond (ξεινήιον, δῶρα).

noncore_FEs.name: Guarantor
noncore_FEs.definition: The deity under whose protection the bond stands (Ζεὺς ξείνιος).

noncore_FEs.name: Duration
noncore_FEs.definition: How long the bond has lasted (παλαιός 'of old').

noncore_FEs.name: Manner
noncore_FEs.definition: The quality of the bond (προσκηδής 'affectionate, caring').

lexical_units.gloss: relation of guest-friendship between persons or states

examples.note: Homer, Iliad 6.215, verified in the AGLDT Iliad treebank. Target ξεῖνος; Partner_2 (Glaucus) is the unexpressed subject of ἐσσι (CNI).
Homer, Odyssey 1.187, verified in the AGLDT Odyssey treebank. Target ξεῖνοι; Partners = 'we', subject of εὐχόμεθ' (CNI), with reciprocal ἀλλήλων.

examples.text: [τῷ|Partner_2] δ' [Ὀδυσεὺς|Partner_1] [ξίφος ὀξὺ καὶ ἄλκιμον ἔγχος|Token] ἔδωκεν, ἀρχὴν ξεινοσύνης [προσκηδέος|Manner]
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 21.34-35, verified in the AGLDT Odyssey treebank. Target ξεινοσύνης; the Partners and the Token are arguments of ἔδωκεν, which here creates the bond.

examples.text: Because of the ξενία between [their fathers|Origin_of_bond], [Glaucus|Partner_1] and [Diomedes|Partner_2] exchanged [armour|Token] instead of fighting.
examples.note: illustrative (English paraphrase of the Iliad 6 episode, not a quotation)

name: Tending
definition: A Caretaker attends, on an ongoing basis, to the needs or condition of a Charge — a person, animal, plant, piece of land, household or livelihood — so as to keep it in good condition or improve its well-being. The Caretaker is often a servant or dependant acting on behalf of an Owner of the Charge. The frame differs from Assistance (help towards a specific Goal of a Benefited_party), from Agriculture (cultivation of Food) and from Cure (healing an Affliction) in profiling continuous care and upkeep rather than a goal, a crop or a cure.

core_FEs.name: Caretaker
core_FEs.definition: The person who looks after the Charge.

core_FEs.name: Charge
core_FEs.definition: The person, animal, plant, land, household or livelihood that is looked after.

noncore_FEs.name: Owner
noncore_FEs.definition: The person to whom the Charge belongs and on whose behalf the Caretaker acts.

noncore_FEs.name: Manner
noncore_FEs.definition: How the tending is done (well, with skill, carelessly).

noncore_FEs.name: Means
noncore_FEs.definition: The action by which the Caretaker tends the Charge.

noncore_FEs.name: Purpose
noncore_FEs.definition: What the Caretaker aims to achieve by the tending.

lexical_units.gloss: tend, look after (orchard, livelihood), busy oneself about
take care of, tend (body, animals, land); post-Homeric in this sense

examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 24.257, verified in the AGLDT Odyssey treebank. Caretaker = 'you' (Laertes), unexpressed subject (CNI).

examples.text: ὦ γέρον, οὐκ ἀδαημονίη [σ'|Caretaker] ἔχει ἀμφιπολεύειν [ὄρχατον|Charge]
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 24.244-245, verified in the AGLDT Odyssey treebank.

examples.text: εἰ [κεῖνός|Caretaker] γ' ἐλθὼν [τὸν ἐμὸν βίον|Charge] ἀμφιπολεύοι
examples.note: Homer, Odyssey 18.254 (= 19.127), verified in the AGLDT Odyssey treebank.
